sum: Three or four easy days below Annapurna South: up to Ghandruk, across the Modi Khola to Landruk and Tolka, over a forested saddle to Dhampus and down the stone steps to Phedi.
reach: By tourist bus (7–9 hours) or by air (about 25 minutes).

guide.note: Since April 2023 the Nepal Tourism Board has required foreign trekkers in conservation areas to walk with a licensed guide, though checks on the trail are inconsistent. The paths on this loop are wide and well signed, so a guide is not there to find the way. He or she earns the fee on the long staircases, by setting a slow, steady pace and lending a hand where the steps are high, and by booking rooms and a jeep when plans change.

access: Jeeps and buses from Pokhara reach Kimche in about three hours by way of Nayapul, and most jeeps carry on to the stand below Ghandruk. The walk ends at Phedi on the Baglung highway, half an hour from Pokhara by taxi or local bus. Dhampus, Landruk and Tolka are on jeep tracks as well, so there is a way out by road from every night's stop.

photo.a: A blue-roofed white building and a farmhouse stand on a grassy terrace above the deep Modi Khola valley, with the snow peaks of Annapurna South and Hiunchuli at its head.
photo.c: Tolka, with Annapurna South and Hiunchuli at the head of the Modi Khola valley

permits.name: Annapurna Conservation Area Permit
permits.where: Online at NTNC's e-permit site, or in person at the Tourist Service Centre in Bhrikutimandap, Kathmandu, and the Nepal Tourism Board office in Pokhara. A permit issued at a trail checkpost costs double.

permits.name: Trekkers' Information Management System card
permits.where: Only through a registered trekking agency, which applies in the Nepal Tourism Board's online system with your route and your guide's details. Individual trekkers can no longer buy one over the counter.

transportText: Tourist bus between Kathmandu and Pokhara both ways, a jeep seat to Kimche, and a taxi back from Phedi shared by two
tips: Carry two trekking poles. They take real weight off the knees on the staircases.
Leave Ghandruk by eight, so that you are up the far side of the valley and in Landruk before the midday heat.
Keep your ACAP permit and TIMS card to hand. They are looked at in Birethanti on the drive in and again at Pothana.
Book rooms ahead in October, November, March and April, and for Friday and Saturday nights in Ghandruk and Dhampus, when visitors from Pokhara fill the lodges.
There is no cash machine on the loop. Bring rupees from Pokhara, with small notes for tea shops.

days.t: Drive to Kimche, walk up to Ghandruk
days.note: About three hours by jeep or bus through Nayapul and Birethanti, where permits are checked. From Kimche an hour of stone steps climbs 300 m between terraces to the village. Jeeps also go on to the stand at the foot of Ghandruk, a short walk below the lodges. Keep the afternoon for the old upper village and the museum.

The day of steps. Go down about 650 m of stone staircase to the suspension bridge over the Modi Khola, an hour to an hour and a half, then climb 270 m to Landruk for lunch. Tolka is another hour along the hillside, partly on the jeep track. Leave early so that the climb out of the valley is done before midday.

days.t: Tolka to Dhampus over Pitam Deurali
days.note: A steady climb of 400 m through oak and rhododendron forest to the saddle at Pitam Deurali, an hour and a half to two hours. From there it is downhill: forty minutes to Pothana, where permits are checked, and an hour or more on a wide path through forest and fields to Dhampus.

days.t: Dhampus to Phedi, drive to Pokhara
days.note: Get up for the sunrise on the range, then walk down through the terraces and a last 500 m of stone steps to the highway at Phedi. Allow an hour and a half if your knees are tired. Taxis and buses reach Pokhara in half an hour or a little more.
